references.text: Joel prophesied that God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh – this is the "Father's promise" (ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρός) which Jesus refers to in [ref:Joel 3:1-2|Joel 3:1-2].

God promises through Isaiah to pour out His Spirit on Israel's offspring: "I will pour out My Spirit on your offspring" – one of the Old Testament promises concerning the gift of the Spirit ([ref:Jes 44:3|Isaiah 44:3]).
Isaiah speaks of the Spirit being poured out from on high (ἐξ ὕψους), which is directly reflected in Jesus' words about being "clothed with power from on high" ([ref:Jes 32:15|Isaiah 32:15]).

Jesus promises the disciples that He will ask the Father, and the Father will give them another Advocate, the Holy Spirit – this elaborates what the "Father's promise" entails ([ref:Joh 14:16-17|John 14:16-17]).

Jesus says that the Father will send the Holy Spirit in His name, who will teach them all things – a further explanation of the promise mentioned in [ref:Luk 24:49|Luke 24:49] ([ref:Joh 14:26|John 14:26]).
Jesus promises to send the Spirit of truth from the Father – parallel to "I will send (ἐξαποστέλλω) the Father's promise upon you" ([ref:Joh 15:26|John 15:26]).
Jesus says that He will send the Advocate to the disciples after His departure – this confirms that it is Jesus Himself who sends the Spirit as promised ([ref:Joh 16:7|John 16:7]).

Luke recounts Jesus' command to wait in Jerusalem for "what the Father has promised" and that they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit – a direct parallel to [ref:Luk 24:49|Luke 24:49] ([ref:Apg 1:4-5|Acts 1:4-5]).
Jesus promises that the disciples will receive power (δύναμιν) when the Holy Spirit comes upon them – the fulfillment of the promise to be "clothed with power from on high" ([ref:Apg 1:8|Acts 1:8]).
On Pentecost, the disciples were filled with the Holy Spirit – the concrete fulfillment of the Father's promise that Jesus spoke about ([ref:Apg 2:1-4|Acts 2:1-4]).

Peter explains that Jesus, exalted at God's right hand, has received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father and poured it out so that what the disciples see and hear is fulfilled – a direct fulfillment of [ref:Luk 24:49|Luke 24:49] ([ref:Apg 2:33|Acts 2:33]).

Paul writes that Abraham's blessing came to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit – the "Father's promise" understood in the context of salvation history ([ref:Gal 3:14|Galatians 3:14]).
